chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback `have = list(prior.globs or (parked.globs if parked is not None else []))` uses `parked` instead of the caller’s own prior live lease when `prior.globs` is empty. `parked` is the existing parked lease, not the lease being renewed, so a live-holder re-claim with an empty prior coverage and a non-None parked lease either inherits the wrong other lease’s globs (for example the previous holder’s `["old.py"]`), or raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` if that parked lease’s `globs` is `None`. The included regression test does not exercise this branch because its `prior.globs` is non-empty, so `parked` is short-circuited away.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression suite covers `LC.claim` with an explicit non-empty `globs="src/mine.py"`, but it never exercises `LC.update` or the CLI `update --globs ""` path. The bug report explicitly says `update --globs ""` cannot opt out, and the manifest only changes `claim.py` and `lifecycle_cli.py` (no `update.py`), so this half of the promised fix is both untested and plausibly still broken: the suite can pass while `ddflow update fix-Bh --globs ""` still takes the bug’s globs and waits on another agent’s lease of `src/h.py`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new terminal-lease skip is guarded by `lease.holder != me`, so a finished item whose lease is held by the current agent is still added to `mine` (and sets `holds_any`). This keeps the commit hook disagreeing with `update` for the agent’s own finished leases, even though the comment says a finished item “holds nothing.” Concrete failure: agent A has terminal unreleased lease `T` with glob `src/**`; A commits `src/foo.py`. The hook does not skip `T`, `_counts_as_mine` returns true, `src/foo.py` is not uncovered, and `_check_lease` returns OK. `update`, which ignores finished holders regardless of holder, does not count `T` as covering `src/foo.py`. The skip should apply to terminal items for all holders, not only when `lease.holder != me`.

chunk_findings.detail: `contested` does not restrict other leases to the committer’s line, even though its own docstring says a path is contested only when “another live, unfinished lease on the same line covers too.” The update path in `ddflow/services/leases.py` computes `line = line_key(state, it, cfg)` and then scans `unfinished_leases` (the loop visible around line 224), which implies it filters out items on other lines; `contested` neither imports nor calls `line_key` and iterates every unfinished lease. Concrete false refusal: item A on line 1 holds wildcard `**/*.txt` and has changed `docs/a.txt`; item B on line 2 stages `docs/a.txt` under its own wildcard lease. Update --globs permits the cross-line overlap, but `contested` sees A’s changed wildcard match and returns `"A (holder)"`, so the commit hook refuses a commit update would allow.

chunk_findings.detail: `contested` loops over `L.unfinished_leases(state, cfg, now)` — every live unfinished lease in the whole state — and never computes or compares `line_key(state, other, cfg)` with the committer’s line. The update-side logic this is supposed to mirror computes `line = line_key(state, it, cfg)` before the same loop and restricts lease clashes to the same line. Concrete failure: committer C has an unfinished item on line A with only a wildcard lease `proj/*`; a different unfinished item on line B has an exact lease `proj/a.txt`. `update --globs` should not treat the line-B lease as a clash, but `contested` sees it (`_holds` returns True for the exact glob) and makes the hook refuse `proj/a.txt`, reintroducing the hook/update disagreement. The function needs the same line-key filter as the update path.
